---
title: PBS and Torque
description: Submit one HTSeq job per sample with qsub.
---

On PBS/Torque, each sample becomes its own `qsub` job. The jobs retain
independent identifiers and logs.

They share the scheduler-neutral manifest format used by the Slurm backend.

```bash
htseq-count-cluster run \
  --scheduler pbs \
  --infile samples.csv \
  --gtf genes.gtf \
  --outpath counts \
  --partition batch \
  --memory 4gb \
  --time 02:00:00
```

HTSeqCountCluster maps its options to PBS arguments:

- `--partition` becomes the `qsub -q` queue name.
- `--account` becomes the `qsub -A` account.
- CPU and memory use `select=1:ncpus=<N>:mem=<MEMORY>`.
- Time uses a separate `walltime=<TIME>` value.

Resource syntax varies among PBS-family installations. Use `--dry-run` and
compare the generated command with the cluster documentation.

## Check status once

```bash
htseq-count-cluster status --scheduler pbs 12345.server
```

The command runs `qstat -f` once and normalizes the PBS state.

If the job is absent from the site's `qstat` history, the result is `Unknown`.
Absence alone does not establish success.
